title: Does a fixed Whittaker function serve as a universal Rankin-Selberg test vector?
question:
Suppose F is a number field and \Pi is a fixed irreducible cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_n(\mathbf{A}_F) with Whittaker model W(\Pi,\psi^{-1}). For any irreducible generic representation \pi of GL_n(\mathbf{A}_F) let \phi_{\pi}(g) be the standard Rankin-Selberg section used together with the prescribed u_Q-twist. Consider

Z(W,\phi_{\pi},s)=\int_{U_Q(\mathbf{A}_F)\backslash GL_n(\mathbf{A}_F)} W(g u_Q)\,\phi_{\pi}(g)\,\delta_Q(g)^s\,dg

with u_Q \in U_Q(\mathbf{A}_F) producing the additive character on the unipotent. Does there exist a single W \in W(\Pi,\psi^{-1}) that acts as a universal test vector so that for every generic \pi and every complex s the integral converges and remains nonzero, or must W inevitably depend on the local ramification of \pi even when \Pi contributes a spherical Whittaker function?
answer:
No such universal W exists. Because Z(W,\phi_{\pi},s) factors as \prod_v Z_v(W_v,\pi_v,s), a fixed global Whittaker function would have to make every local factor nonzero for every generic representation \pi_v of GL_n(F_v). Inside the Kirillov model each local component satisfies

Z_v(W_v,\pi_v,s)=\int_{F_v^{\times}} W_v(a(t))\,|t|_v^{s+(n-1)/2}\,\chi_{\pi_v}(t)^{-1}\,dt,

so W_v(a(t)) is a smooth compactly supported function of v_v(t). Let c(\pi_v) be the ramification conductor. If c(\pi_v) exceeds the valuation window where W_v(a(t)) is nonzero, one can twist a fixed unramified representation by a character of conductor c(\pi_v) so that the oscillation of \chi_{\pi_v} forces this integral to vanish identically for every s. That single zero kills the global Euler product, showing there is no pi-independent Whittaker test vector. The u_Q-twist only inserts a fixed additive character along U_Q and does not alter the diagonal Mellin transform, so it cannot rescue the highly ramified cases. What actually holds, via the Jacquet-Piatetski-Shapiro-Shalika test-vector theorem, is that for each \pi there exists an "essential" Whittaker vector W_{\Pi,\pi} matched to c(\pi_v) at every v, and these give the correct Rankin-Selberg factors. Therefore the fixed-W universality claim fails: obtaining finite, nonzero u_Q-twisted integrals requires varying W with \pi, typically by using the local newforms in the Kirillov model aligned with the ramification conductor.
